name: variable_speed_pump_simulation
title: Variable-speed pump from dimensionless polynomials
summary: Predicts the head, speed, shaft power and electrical power of a centrifugal pump on a quadratic system curve, using catalogue cubics of the dimensionless head and power coefficients and part-load motor and VFD efficiencies. Water enters only through the suction density.

verification.summary: compare_solution.py --ees-units: 26 common variables, 0 differ (rtol=0.001); only in EES: 0; only in CoolSolve: 2. Maximum relative difference 2.55e-05 on W_dot_elec_p. rho_su_p, DELTAP_p and W_dot_shaft_p differ by 2.54e-05 because CoolProp water at 20 °C and 101300 Pa is 998.207 kg/m3 against the stored 998.233 kg/m3. verification.notes: 26 common variables, none above rtol=0.001. The largest relative difference the tool prints is 2.55e-05 on W_dot_elec_p (exact ratio 2.546e-05). rho_su_p, DELTAP_p and W_dot_shaft_p are 2.54e-05. CoolProp density of Water at 20 °C and 101300 Pa is 998.207139 kg/m3; the stored rho_su_p is 998.2325392 kg/m3. Head is K*V_dot^2 and the speed loop uses psi = g*H/(omega^2*D^2), so H_p, psi_p, phi_p and omega_p match. Shaft and electrical power scale with density. --ees-units prints: Converted EES reference values: P_w_su_p (kPa x1000), W_dot_motor_nom_p (kW x1000). DELTAP_p, W_dot_shaft_p and W_dot_elec_p have empty stored unit strings and are already in Pa and W (about 245572 Pa, 4790 W and 5831 W); they are not scaled. No stored unit is kj or KJ. Names only in the CoolSolve solution: pi and W_dot_motor_nom_kW_p.
